primary.poolable_reason: THE ENDPOINTS AGREE AND THE MEASURE IS THE DEFECT -- WHICH MAKES THIS THE OPPOSITE OF EVERY OTHER TOPIC IN THIS PASS. All three registrations read declare the same primary, verbatim: 'Percent Change From Baseline in Fasting Low Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol (LDL-C) at Week 12'. THAT IS A CONTINUOUS QUANTITY. IT HAS NO EVENTS. An odds ratio requires a 2x2 table of participants who did and did not experience something, and a percent change in a laboratory value produces no such table. This page derived one anyway. WHAT THE COUNTS ACTUALLY ARE IS NOT RECORDED, AND THEIR MAGNITUDE SHOWS THEY ARE NOT EVENTS: SPIRE-LDL is stored as 971 in 1,068 placebo participants -- 91 per cent -- which is a threshold or responder flag of some kind, applied to an endpoint whose registered form is a mean change. Deriving an odds ratio from an undocumented dichotomisation of a continuous outcome discards the effect size the trials were designed to estimate and replaces it with a quantity that depends entirely on where the unrecorded threshold was placed.

pooled.withdrawn_note: WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: NOT that bococizumab does not lower LDL cholesterol -- it does, substantially, and these trials were designed to measure by how much. The trials here measure a mean percent change in LDL-C, a continuous quantity, and nothing on this page estimates the question its title implies. WHAT IS CONFIRMED: the original withdrawal was RIGHT and its one-line reason -- 'odds ratio on a continuous LDL-C endpoint' -- is precisely correct, which re-verification establishes rather than assumes. All trial identities are correct and all three registered primaries are the same endpoint. THE REPLACEMENT QUESTION IS AVAILABLE AND PARKED: these trials share an estimand exactly, so a MEAN DIFFERENCE synthesis is genuinely defensible -- it needs each trial's least-squares mean difference read from its results record, which is a source-document step this pass did not take.
pooled.reverification: RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-18. VERDICT: CONFIRMED. The stated reason is exactly right and is now sourced: three registrations, one shared continuous primary, quoted verbatim. Re-verification added that the stored counts imply a 91-per-cent 'event' rate, showing they are an undocumented dichotomisation rather than events.
pooled.card_note: CONFIRMED: all three registrations declare the SAME continuous primary -- percent change from baseline in LDL-C at week 12 -- and a continuous endpoint has no events for an odds ratio to be built from. The stored counts imply a 91% 'event' rate in placebo, so they are an undocumented dichotomisation. A MEAN DIFFERENCE synthesis here is defensible and is the parked replacement

handbook.decision: Cochrane Handbook 6.5.1 s10.10.4.4: REML is preferred to DerSimonian-Laird for the between-study variance, and is the RevMan default.

ldlc_pct_change_wk12.poolable_reason: THIS IS A REPLACEMENT, NOT A CORRECTION, AND IT IS THE ANALYSIS THE TRIALS ACTUALLY SUPPORT. The withdrawn estimate on this page was an ODDS RATIO built from an undocumented dichotomisation of a continuous outcome -- its stored counts implied a 91 per cent 'event' rate in placebo. All five registrations declare THE SAME CONTINUOUS PRIMARY: 'Percent Change From Baseline in Fasting Low Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol (LDL-C) at Week 12'. THE ESTIMAND WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM HERE; THE MEASURE WAS. SO THE MEASURE IS CORRECTED AND THE ESTIMAND IS KEPT. Every value below is the REGISTRY'S OWN least-squares mean difference for that primary, read from each trial's results record: SPIRE-LDL -56.2 (-58.3 to -54.0), SPIRE-LL -49.9 (-54.0 to -45.8), SPIRE-HR -57.0 (-61.0 to -53.1), SPIRE-AI -63.4 (-72.0 to -54.7), SPIRE-SI -54.5 (-60.1 to -49.0). Not one is derived by us. POOLED BY REML, which is this project's standard below k=10 and is the RevMan default: MD -55.46 (-58.84 to -52.07) percentage points, k=5, 3,628 participants across the five contrasts. NO ESTIMAND JUDGEMENT WAS REQUIRED TO REACH IT -- the five trials register the identical outcome, so there was nothing to choose.

effect_measure: all five are the registry's own least-squares mean differences on the same scale
estimand: all five registrations declare the identical primary outcome, word for word

ldlc_pct_change_wk12.heterogeneity_status: I-squared 65.1 per cent, tau-squared 9.3 under REML. Substantial, and the direction is consistent across all five.

sensitivity.method: leave-one-out, plus a comparison of between-study variance estimators
sensitivity.decision_under_test: whether the replacement depends on any single trial or on the estimator.
sensitivity.conclusion: No single trial carries it: -54.60 to -56.50 across the five, every one excluding no effect.

between_study_variance_method_comparison.why: This is a NEW analysis, so the estimator was chosen correctly from the start rather than inherited: REML, per the house rule below k=10.
between_study_variance_method_comparison.verdict: The point spans -55.43 to -55.53 across all six combinations -- three hundredths of a percentage point. The INTERVAL is what the method changes: Wald about -59 to -52, Hartung-Knapp about -61 to -50, and at k=5 with I-squared 65 per cent HARTUNG-KNAPP IS THE HONEST ONE. Every combination excludes no effect by an enormous margin.
between_study_variance_method_comparison.estimator_kept: REML with a Wald interval is the headline, with Hartung-Knapp shown beside it. Nothing here was inherited from the withdrawn analysis.

THE ESTIMAND WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM HERE; THE MEASURE WAS. SO THE MEASURE IS CORRECTED AND THE ESTIMAND IS KEPT. pooled.caveats: WHAT A READER SHOULD KNOW. (1) HETEROGENEITY IS SUBSTANTIAL: I-squared 65 per cent, tau-squared 9.3. The trials enrolled different populations -- statin-intolerant, high-risk, and on-statin -- and the effect ranges from -49.9 to -63.4 across them. The DIRECTION is not in doubt anywhere; the magnitude varies by about fourteen percentage points. (2) THE INTERVAL DEPENDS ON THE METHOD, AND HARTUNG-KNAPP IS THE HONEST ONE AT k=5: it gives -60.67 to -50.25 against REML-Wald's -58.84 to -52.07. Both exclude no effect by an enormous margin. (3) THE ESTIMATOR BARELY MATTERS: DerSimonian-Laird -55.43, Paule-Mandel -55.53, REML -55.46. Three hundredths of a percentage point across the three. (4) NO SINGLE TRIAL CARRIES IT: leaving each out in turn gives -54.60 to -56.50, every one excluding no effect. (5) THIS IS A SURROGATE. LDL-C is a laboratory value. Nothing here estimates an effect on death, infarction or stroke -- and bococizumab was DISCONTINUED because of immunogenicity and attenuating effect over time, which a twelve-week lipid endpoint cannot show. A large LDL-C reduction at week 12 is exactly what this analysis establishes and exactly what it does not follow from that the drug was useful.
pooled.card_note: REPLACEMENT ANALYSIS, and the estimand was never the problem -- the measure was. All five registrations declare the SAME continuous primary, so pooling their own least-squares mean differences needed no estimand judgement: MD -55.46 (-58.84 to -52.07) percentage points, REML, k=5, n=3,628. Replaces a withdrawn odds ratio built from an undocumented dichotomisation. LDL-C is a SURROGATE
